newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber close mostly up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber close mostly up on short covering.

text.p: Short-covering encouraged by a somewhat better than expected U.S. housing starts report kept CME lumber futures mostly higher at the close, traders said.
Lumber closed $6.70 per tbf higher to 0.100 lower with July up most at $398.50 and September up $5.90 at $387.60.

The housing report showed a 2.6 percent increase in April starts compared with expectations of a small decline. However, the report was tempered by the fact the largest increase in starts came in multi-family units, traders said.
Also limiting the advance in futures were reports of continued weakness in cash lumber.
"Activity has to increase or prices need to come down," one cash source said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $382, off $2 from both midweek and week ago levels.
